Inspect and manage the cached test data

Source: R/testdata.R
gsm_testdata.Rd

Usage

gsm_testdata(cache = getOption("gsm.testdata_cache"))

Arguments

cache

cachem A cachem cache to use from now on. Defaults to the gsm.testdata_cache option; NULL keeps the current cache. A new cache is also stored in that option for the rest of the session. Objects already loaded this session stay in memory; later loads use the new cache.

Value

FreshHandle An R6 object with

  • key(): the release tag currently in use.

  • refresh(): choose the release again now.

  • reset(): forget the release choice, so the next access re-resolves everything. Cached values are kept.

  • set_cache(cache): switch caches without changing the option.

  • cache: the current cachem object. Use its methods directly, e.g. gsm_testdata()$cache$size(), $keys(), $prune(), $reset() (delete all cached values), or $destroy().

  • state: the store that records the chosen release; state$path shows where it's saved.

  • snapshot: the local folder in use (see use_testdata_snapshot()), or NULL.

Details

The test data objects (e.g. analyticsInput) are cached in a standard cachem cache. gsm_testdata() returns a handle for inspecting and managing the cache, and can be used to switch to a different cache.

To change where or how values are cached, see use_testdata_cache_dir().

Examples

handle <- gsm_testdata()
handle
#> A fresh handle
#> • Current key: "data-8cde53949d4d"
#> • Cache: <cache_disk/cachem>
#> • State: /home/runner/.cache/R/gsm/testdata-state.rds
#> • Snapshot: '(none)'
handle$cache$info()
#> $dir
#> [1] "/home/runner/.cache/R/gsm/values"
#> 
#> $max_size
#> [1] 1073741824
#> 
#> $max_age
#> [1] Inf
#> 
#> $max_n
#> [1] Inf
#> 
#> $evict
#> [1] "lru"
#> 
#> $destroy_on_finalize
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $missing
#> <quosure>
#> expr: ^key_missing()
#> env:  0x5bdb7b384118
#> 
#> $prune_rate
#> [1] 20
#> 
#> $logfile
#> NULL
#> 
#> $prune_throttle_counter
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $prune_last_time
#> [1] "2026-11-09 22:40:29 UTC"
#> 

# Switch to a temporary in-memory cache, then back.
old <- handle$cache
gsm_testdata(cache = cachem::cache_mem())
#> A fresh handle
#> • Current key: "data-8cde53949d4d"
#> • Cache: <cache_mem/cachem>
#> • State: /home/runner/.cache/R/gsm/testdata-state.rds
#> • Snapshot: '(none)'
gsm_testdata(cache = old)
#> A fresh handle
#> • Current key: "data-8cde53949d4d"
#> • Cache: <cache_disk/cachem>
#> • State: /home/runner/.cache/R/gsm/testdata-state.rds
#> • Snapshot: '(none)'
